findings.text: retry_failures is a list whose entries a guard consumes one at a time (reports.py:1056 counted_retry_failures; reports.py:2352 reads retry_failures as a list and reports.py:2446 tests membership as set(retry_failures) & after_ids), so by the membership rule the widened comment states at reports.py:98-107 it belongs in _GUARDED_LIST_KEYS and does not; probed read-only at the reviewed head, parse_manifest('...\nretry_failures: tests/a.py::t1; tests/b.py::t2\n') is ACCEPTED as ['tests/a.py::t1; tests/b.py::t2'], one entry matching neither id, so a joined retry-failure list silently under-counts the retries the stop rule counts. Not a regression against this delta's base (5eb4dd58 refused retry_failures no more than it refused test_logs or commits) and the entry-token predicate would already refuse it if the field were listed, so it does not hold the node.

_COMMIT_IDENTIFIER_TOKEN = re.compile(r"[0-9a-fA-F]{7,40}") duplicates the commit-identifier pattern the same module already owns at reports.py:1260 (_RECORDED_REVISION, [0-9a-fA-F]{7,64}, used at reports.py:1301 and reports.py:1973) and beside _HEAD_KEYED_RECORD_NAME/_HEAD_KEYED_SUFFIX at reports.py:1624/2515; the addition neither extends nor wraps that owner, it adds a fifth near-identical hex-identifier regex with an arbitrarily narrower upper bound. The mechanism the constant serves (_looks_like_a_list_entry_token, reports.py:835) does extend the existing owner _refuse_joined_list_separator (reports.py:869), which is why this is scored as a lexical duplication rather than a forked capability, and it is recorded rather than held.
